content.comment_body: Hello, I've purchased several [product_name] modules for use in a master/slave arrangement. My main module is a [product_name] as master, and two [product_name] modules as slaves. I plan to connect all three using a [product_name] communication module. Currently, I can't connect my laptop to the two slave modules since I can't determine their correct IP addresses (these slaves don't have a display, so I can't verify the IPs directly). This is preventing successful testing. I am able to connect to and transfer a program to one slave module from my laptop. How do I connect to both slave modules and locate their IP addresses? Thank you for responding quickly.

Welcome to the forum. There are a few ways you could address your issue. The simplest way is to create a small program—such as toggling an output with an input—and set your desired IP address, subnet mask, and gateway in the project properties, along with the correct hardware type. Save this program as a .bin file, and copy it to an mSD card formatted with FAT32. Insert the card into the [product_name] device and restart it. The module should then adopt the IP settings from the mSD card, and you can remove the card afterward.
Alternatively, you can open a network project, select "Go Online" from the menu, and use the LSC tool to scan for all reachable [product_name] modules and display their IP addresses.
Thank you. I noticed that two modules have the same IP address. Will they be able to communicate with each other?

No, it's not possible to connect to two devices with the same IP address. Disconnect the ethernet cable from one, then open LSC and navigate to Tools > Transfer > Configure Network Address, where you can change the IP address. Afterwards, connect and adjust the IP address for the other module.
Thanks, but I'm having trouble changing the address (see attachment). If I try to edit it in the provided field, I still can't connect.
It works for me without issues—see the attached screen recording. After entering the new address, did you press the "Assign IP address" button?
What IP address and subnet mask does your laptop currently use?
Whenever I try to transfer the program from my laptop to the slave module, I keep seeing the same window. I'm getting confused...

Let's go back to basics. Which [product_name] modules do you have? Please provide the full [article_no]s. Also, which LSC [version_no] are you running? What's your laptop's IP address and subnet mask?
No worries, we'll sort this out, but I need all the details.
Subnet mask: 0.0.0.0
[product_name] + [product_name] ([version_no]) + 5 modules [product_name]. Do you need more info?
LSC [version_no]
As mentioned earlier, please provide the full [article_no]s. Also, why does your laptop have a subnet mask of 0.0.0.0? That's unusual...
[article_no]: 6ED1 055-1NB10-0BA2 [article_no]: 6ED1 052-1MD08-0BA0 [article_no]: 6ED1 052-2MD08-0BA1 [article_no]: 6GK7177-1MA20-0AA0
I changed my subnet mask to 192.168.0.10—it was set to 0.0.0.0 by default. I don't know much about networking.
Still unable to access the remote device...
For these modules ([version_no]), you need to use LSC [version_no]. Please check your device's packaging to confirm.

You can download the upgrade to LSC [version_no] from here: [url]. However, the download is restricted—you'll need to register for access. For the company field, enter "private using" if you're not representing a business.
Thank you for explaining. I haven't had power at home for two days. Is it possible to get the download link quickly?

No, your data will be checked first. If approved, you'll get a download email, but since it's the weekend, the company won't process it until next Thursday or Friday at the earliest. Without LSC [version_no], you can't switch the modules to slave mode since these versions lack a display.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter obstacles when configuring and networking multiple [product_name] modules without a display, mainly due to challenges in identifying and setting IP addresses. Duplicate defaults and limited feedback from tools result in significant confusion, slowing the commissioning process in multi-device scenarios.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy way to discover, assign, and change IP addresses on multiple display-less modules, along with reliable program transfers from a laptop.
